```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

Start here to read two fictional uploads, create the two cache levels, run QC,
and inspect a saved result. Each tutorial is self-contained and uses
`data(appusage_demo)` or its bundled TXT files. File-writing examples use a
temporary directory and one worker.

## Find the shared inputs

```{r inputs}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "synth", package = "appusageR", mustWork = TRUE)
chosen <- appusage_demo$sources$scenario %in% c("line_seven_days", "meta_seven_days")
sources <- appusage_demo$sources[chosen, ]
paths <- file.path(folder, sources$source_relpath)
sources[, c("sequence_id", "scenario", "expected_status")]
```

ProjectID `"009"` and the upload sequences are character identifiers. The source
guide `?appusage_synthetic_project` describes all 15 uploads, including five
deliberately invalid inputs. `?appusage_demo` describes the ten successful records
and the 17-row fictional survey.

## Plan and run

```{r workflow}
work <- tempfile("appusage-start-")
config <- appusage_config(
  time = list(tz = appusage_demo$info$timezone),
  execution = list(parallel = FALSE, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE))
plan <- plan_appusage_workflow(paths, work, config)
plan$tasks[, c("stage", "action", "reason_code")]
result <- run_appusage_workflow(plan = plan)
summary(result)$overview$execution
stopifnot(nrow(result$first_level) == 2L,
          all(result$first_level$status == "success"),
          all(result$second_level$second_level_status == "success"),
          all(result$qc$pass_qc))
```

```{r flow, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(system.file("figures", "workflow.svg", package = "appusageR"))
```

`proc-1` holds faithful parsed data. `proc-2` holds standardized research tables;
its paired JSON owns routine QC and category metadata. Use
`?appusage_configuration` for defaults, units, accepted values and stage scope.

## Inspect one saved source

Load each RDA into its own environment. Every cache owns one object named `data`.

```{r inspect}
pair <- result$second_level[1L, ]
cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
stopifnot(identical(load(pair$second_level_data_file, envir = cache), "data"))
vapply(cache$data, nrow, integer(1))
head(cache$data$daily[, c("date", "app_name", "duration_ms")])
metadata <- jsonlite::read_json(pair$second_level_metadata_file, simplifyVector = TRUE)
names(metadata)
result$qc[, c("participant_id", "qc_status", "pass_qc")]
delivery <- validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content")
stopifnot(isTRUE(delivery$complete))
print(delivery)
```

| Result | Meaning | Unit or denominator | Empty or failed state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first_level$status` | Source parsing outcome | Each selected upload | Diagnosed input failures keep a row |
| `event`, `episode`, `daily` | Different views of one source | Events, intervals, app-days | Unavailable grains are typed zero-row tables |
| `duration_ms` | Recorded duration | Milliseconds; divide by 60,000 for minutes | Missing is distinct from zero |
| `qc_status` | Whether QC ran | Sources reaching QC | Upstream failures are not evaluated |
| `pass_qc` | Existing coverage/quality rule | Evaluated sources | Separate from grain-specific eligibility |
| `delivery$complete` | Required artifacts and diagnoses are accounted for | All selected sources | Can include diagnosed input failures |

Both selected sources meet the existing seven-day QC rule. The
[QC tutorial](day-and-overlap-audits.html) adds short-coverage examples. The
[project tutorial](projects-and-surveys.html) retains all 15 uploads and constructs
a second project in which all five inputs fail.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```

Next: [formats and data model](formats-and-data-model.html).
Open `?appusageR` for the six-task navigation and `demo("synthetic-project",
package = "appusageR", ask = FALSE)` for the full project with two file workers.
